@graph.name: Property management for owners
@graph.description: Leasing, tenant screening, maintenance coordination and owner reporting for rental property in Texas.

acceptedAnswer.text: Management fees are typically a percentage of collected rent, with a separate leasing fee when a new tenant is placed. Both are quoted in writing for your specific property before you commit — we do not publish a single rate because unit type, condition and location genuinely change the work involved.
You set a dollar threshold. Work below it proceeds so routine issues do not stall; anything above it comes to you for approval first.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a tenant stops paying?

acceptedAnswer.text: We follow the notice and escalation process Texas law requires, keep you informed at each stage, and coordinate counsel if it proceeds to eviction. Consistent documentation from move-in is what makes that process work.

mainEntity.name: Do you manage properties outside Dallas-Fort Worth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Seeto Realty works across both the Dallas-Fort Worth and Greater Houston markets, with agents covering the Houston side.
